dedupe_keys.name: broadland flood alleviation project soft and hard engineering in the norfolk broads uk

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes the Broadland Flood Alleviation Project, a 20-year programme to reduce tidal flood risk in the Norfolk Broads, East Anglia, UK, a wetland of rivers and lakes around the tidal Yare, Waveney and Bure. Peat and clay embankments had settled and were eroded by boat wash, so that by the early 1990s even modest surges could overtop or breach them; sea level rise was expected to worsen this. The low-lying land is divided into 40 flood compartments, and works combined bank raising and strengthening, set-back of banks, and erosion protection with softer measures. Improvement works ran from 2001 to 2016 and maintenance to 2021, at an expected total of 136 million pounds, 107.7 million for construction and 31.3 million for maintenance, delivered through a Private Finance Initiative contract in which the Environment Agency delegated flood risk functions to Broadland Environmental Services. The page is free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal. Caveats: the project was cost-limited, figures are expected totals, and after 2021 assets pass to routine maintenance. It illustrates investment appraisal and design of regional flood defences under sea level rise; a related record is the Physical Vulnerability Database for critical infrastructure.
name: Broadland Flood Alleviation Project, soft and hard engineering in the Norfolk Broads (UK)
outcomes: Flood banks across 40 compartments were improved from 2001 to 2016 at an expected total cost of 136 million pounds, with maintenance to 2021.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study on the Environment Agency Broadland Flood Alleviation Project
